D: A stock car racing star loses everything to a French rival and has to fight his way back.
P: Serve the mains when Ricky says grace over the family dinner.
S: Franks dipped in buttermilk cornmeal batter and fried deep golden, with mustard
Franks on sticks dipped in a batter of cornmeal, flour, sugar, egg and buttermilk, fried at 180C for 4 minutes until deep golden. Yellow mustard.
Jean Girard's ham and cheese crêpes
Thin crêpes, some folded around ham and gruyère, some with sugar and lemon
Thin crêpe batter rested an hour, cooked in a buttered pan, folded around ham and gruyère, or sugar and lemon.

Raw peanuts in the shell boiled soft in a salty Cajun brine with garlic and chilli, left to soak up the spice, served warm in paper cups. Rinse 500g raw peanuts in the shell. Put in a large pot with 3L water, 80g salt, 2 tbsp Cajun seasoning, a halved garlic bulb and 2 dried chillies. Weigh down with a plate so they stay under and simmer for 2 hours until soft. Turn off the heat and leave to soak for 1 hour. Drain and serve warm in paper cups with a bowl for shells.
M: Fried chicken, pizza and tacos dinner
Buttermilk fried chicken, homemade pizza and hard shell tacos, Bobby family style
A big family takeaway spread made at home: buttermilk fried chicken, a pizza and hard-shell tacos, all on the table at once. Grace optional.

Pork shoulder rubbed with paprika and brown sugar, slow roasted until it falls apart, tossed in tangy vinegar sauce, on soft rolls with coleslaw and pickles. Mix 2 tbsp paprika, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp cayenne and 2 tsp salt and rub over a 1.5kg pork shoulder. Roast covered at 150C for 5 hours until it pulls apart. Simmer 125ml cider vinegar, 80ml tomato sauce and 1 tbsp brown sugar for 3 minutes and toss through the shredded pork. Toss half a shredded cabbage with mayo. Pile into 8 soft rolls with slaw and pickles.
W: Fudgy dark chocolate brownies, every second square dusted white like a flag
Fudgy brownies baked at 170C for 25 minutes, cut into squares, half dusted with icing sugar in a chequered pattern.
K: Double espresso over ice and milk with homemade salted caramel

Cold milk and homemade salted caramel over ice, with a double espresso poured on top so it layers, finished with a caramel drizzle. Heat 100g caster sugar in a pan until amber, then carefully whisk in 80ml cream, 20g butter and a pinch of salt and cool. Brew 4 double espressos. Spoon 1 tbsp caramel into each of four glasses, fill with ice and add 200ml cold milk. Pour the espresso slowly over the back of a spoon so it layers, then drizzle with more caramel.

s.note: Franks dipped in buttermilk cornmeal batter and fried deep golden, with mustard
s.how: Whisk 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 egg and 250ml buttermilk. Pat 8 franks dry and push onto sticks. Dip and fry at 180C for 4 minutes until deep golden. Serve with mustard.

s.n: Jean Girard's ham and cheese crêpes
s.note: Thin crêpes, some folded around ham and gruyère, some with sugar and lemon
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 eggs and 375ml milk and rest an hour. Cook thin crêpes in a buttered pan. Fold half around 100g ham and 100g gruyère and warm until melted. Sprinkle the rest with sugar and lemon.

m.n: Fried chicken, pizza and tacos dinner
m.note: Buttermilk fried chicken, homemade pizza and hard shell tacos, Bobby family style
m.how: Fry 1kg buttermilk-brined chicken pieces dredged in seasoned flour at 165C until cooked. Bake a 500g pizza dough base with sauce and 200g mozzarella. Brown 400g beef mince with taco spices and fill 8 hard shells. Put it all out together.

w.note: Fudgy dark chocolate brownies, every second square dusted white like a flag
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes and cool. Cut into squares and dust every second one with icing sugar like a chequered flag.

d.note: Double espresso over ice and milk with homemade salted caramel

Spoon 1 tbsp caramel into each of four glasses, fill with ice and add 200ml cold milk. Pour the espresso slowly over the back of a spoon so it layers, then drizzle with more caramel.
